data.title: Something Borrowed
data.rumour: Carmen Ruiz is eloping. Her mother doesn't know.
about: An October story. Carmen Ruiz is eloping with Danny Pacheco on the deck at Dot's Clam Shack, and everyone knows but her mother. She pawns her grandmother's wedding veil for the deposit, mostly so it won't be in the cedar chest when her mother looks (§{carmenVeil}). Her mother, Inés, comes in knowing the veil is gone (§{inesVeil}): tell her about the wedding, keep Carmen's secret, or sell her the veil out from under the loan (Veil for Sale).

At the wedding (§{veilWedding}) bring the veil back to Carmen or just watch. If you told Inés, she turns up, says her own mother married in that veil on a fishing boat in the rain, and pins it on Carmen herself, provided you brought it (Something Old). Otherwise Carmen marries with or without the veil (Elopement).
data.notes: carmenWed and carmenBride are Carmen on her wedding day, without and with the veil.

veil.name: Lace veil
tells: Brussels lace, hand-made, with a darn near the hem in three different threads.
A label sewn inside the band: "Lucía 1952 - Inés 1984 -" and a space.

text: Have you heard? "Carmen Ruiz is eloping, and her mother doesn't know." That's me. Hi. Everyone in town knows except my mother.
Danny and I are getting married on the deck at Dot's Clam Shack. His cousin is a notary. The deposit for the deck is the problem.
This was my grandmother's veil. Then my mother's. Lend me eighty on it? I'll buy it back after. I just need it to not be in my mother's cedar chest when she goes looking.

then.text: Thank you. Day after tomorrow... no. The day after that. Noon, on the deck. You should come. Somebody from my side should be there.

then.toast: Calendar: a wedding at Dot's Clam Shack

else.text: No. You're right. I'll sell my bike. Danny's bike. Somebody's bike.

inesVeil.title: Inés Ruiz knows the veil is gone

text: Inés Ruiz. My daughter has been in here. Don't look at the floor, everybody looks at the floor.
My mother's veil is gone from the cedar chest. Carmen thinks I don't know what the deck at Dot's costs to rent. I know what everything in this town costs.

choose.label: Tell her about the wedding on the deck

text: Noon. On a deck. Over the water. In October.
...She always did hate a fuss. So did I, once. Thank you.

then.text: Hm. Loyal. To her, at least. Good.

choose.label: Let her buy the veil out from under the loan

then.note: The loan and the veil go, and the wedding errand is off.

then.why: Sold Carmen's pawned veil to her mother

then.text: Good. It goes back in the chest. She can have it at a proper wedding. With a priest. And me.

steps.note: Paper flowers on the trellis at the rail.

steps.narrate: Noon at Dot's. Somebody has wound paper flowers round a trellis at the rail. There are eleven guests, a notary in a fishing vest, and a gull with designs on the cake.

choose.label: Just sit at a picnic table and watch

then.text: You brought it? You BROUGHT it. Danny, hold this. Hold everything.
Your grandmother was married in that. On a fishing boat. In the rain. Don't let anyone tell you a deck is worse.

then.narrate: Inés pins the veil herself. Her hands are steadier than the notary's. Afterwards she writes something on the label inside the band, after her own name, and doesn't show anyone.

narrate.then: Carmen is married in her grandmother's veil, on a deck over the harbor, with a gull watching. It is a very good wedding.
narrate.else: Carmen is married bareheaded, on a deck over the harbor, with a gull watching. It is a good wedding anyway.

then.text: And here: from the gift envelope. It's yours, it was always going to be yours.

errands.title: Carmen and Danny's wedding
errands.where: the deck at Dot's Clam Shack

mornings.note: You stayed open: they're married anyway. If the veil sells later, that's the ending that sticks.

then.toast: Carmen Ruiz married Danny Pacheco on the deck at Dot's yesterday. Her grandmother's veil is still on your shelf.
